structured_output.world_model: Time ≈ fixed ~0.1 s + steps × per-step cost, with a large memory-bound share on the 31×31 stem maps. Tip E036 (5.31 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0–2) has a population mean of ~0.752–0.753. The 3-seed accuracy SE is ~0.12 pp, which is as large as most effects. Recipe-level tweaks of averaging, LS and warmup were null or negative. Step trims cost about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. The only free levers are systems work or math-identical changes, and those are worth ≲2%. BN recalibration is a math-changing booster with a plausible small gain. Changing the batch size re-rolls the RNG and is probably neutral to slightly negative at fixed epochs. More steps cost time, and I expect the gain to be under the cost.

forecasts.reason: The Lookahead EMA already averages BN stats. Recalibration likely gives +0.0–0.1 pp, costing ~0.05 s for K=1 to 3 forwards. The seeds 0–2 result will be noisy.
Double the 20 px steps adds ~0.1 s of overhead. The accuracy gain is uncertain, and the RNG re-roll adds noise.
~33% more steps cost ~0.4 s. The accuracy gain is maybe +0.2 pp. This is likely no better than the epoch dial.
The deeper freeze hit a cliff in E037. Saving ~0.1 s likely costs ≥0.15 pp.
This is a diagnostic with no recipe change. Profiling will likely show the stem to be memory-bound and inefficient.
The E031 rate of ~2.3 s/pp applied to a 5% dose gives −0.13 pp, which pushes the mean below the bar.
Math-identical padding aligns Cin to the tensor-core tiles. It likely saves 0–3%, and accuracy is near-identical apart from kernel numerics.

cruxes: Is conv1 (Cin=24, 31×31) actually inefficient? If so, padding gives a free ≥2%, otherwise systems levers are exhausted.
Does BN recalibration after Lookahead add ≥0.1 pp? It is the only unexplored booster that could fund trims.
Does a smaller batch (1500) buy accuracy more cheaply than the epoch dial's ~1.5–2.5 s/pp?
